title: Peppermint fudge
subtitle: peppermint-flavoured condensed milk fudge
excerpt: Peppermint fudge is a clean, cool, sweet confection made from the condensed milk method, which produces a reliably soft, creamy set without thermometers or precise sugar stages. The peppermint extract is added off the heat so it stays sharp and bright. It slices into neat squares that are firm enough to wrap individually. Good for tins and gifts.
sourceNotes: Peppermint fudge is a British confectionery tradition, closely related to Edinburgh mint fudge and the peppermint creams made across Scotland and northern England. The condensed milk fudge method, as opposed to the traditional cream-and-sugar thermometer method, became widespread in British domestic cooking from the mid-20th century, appearing in Women's Institute and school cookery book recipes. Peppermint oil was historically used as the flavouring; modern recipes use peppermint extract, which is more controllable in strength.

recipe.freezeNotes: Wrap in parchment and foil; freeze for up to 3 months. Defrost in the fridge overnight.
recipe.batchNotes: Keeps in an airtight container in the fridge for up to 2 weeks.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Make up to 2 weeks ahead; flavour intensifies slightly on day 2.

content.text: Peppermint fudge uses the condensed milk method, which gives a reliably creamy, soft-set result without thermometers. The mint flavour is sharp and clean against the sweetness, start with less extract and taste, as peppermint extract varies significantly in strength between brands.

items.prepNote: start with 1 tsp; add more to taste

content.text: Combine the condensed milk, butter, and milk in a medium saucepan over a medium heat. Stir to melt the butter. Bring to a gentle simmer, stirring constantly, and cook for 10 minutes. The mixture will thicken and turn a slightly deeper colour. Reduce the heat if it catches on the base. Remove from the heat.

Add the sifted icing sugar in three additions, beating well after each. The mixture will become very stiff and difficult to stir as the sugar goes in. Add the peppermint extract and the food colouring if using, and beat again. Taste and add more extract if needed, peppermint extract varies in strength between brands. Work quickly; the fudge stiffens as it cools.

Tip the mixture into a 20 cm square tin lined with parchment. Press flat with the back of a spoon or a lightly oiled piece of parchment. Refrigerate for 2 hours until firm. Lift out by the parchment and cut into small squares with a sharp knife. Keep in an airtight container in the fridge for up to 2 weeks.
